complete_mirror_norm_proof: For primitive r=(x,y), let I(r)=(a*x,(y,D24+)). Since D24+ is even unimodular, I(r) is a unit away from primes dividing a. Reflection integrality gives (q(r))|2I(r), so no other prime can divide q. At the odd squarefree prime p=(2-theta), either y is primitive and v_p(q)=0, or y lies in pD24+, x is a unit, and q=-a*x^2 mod p^2 has v_p(q)=1. At inert (2), evenness gives y^2 in (2). If a is odd, x a 2-adic unit gives v_2(q)=0, while x in (2) and primitive y gives v_2(q)=1. If a has v_2(a)=1, the whole form is even and the same congruence plus q|2I forces v_2(q)=1. Class number one and U^+=U^2 turn these ideal classes into the displayed totally-positive element representatives. Here a is odd with squarefree support p=(2-theta), so the complete canonical norms are 1, 2, delta, and 2*delta.

delta_divisible_level_reduction.statement: For q=delta or 2*delta, reflection integrality and the self-duality of D24+ force y in delta*D24+. Hence y=delta*z is enumerated exactly at z^2=target/delta^2; a nonintegral reduced target proves that level empty without a spatial search.
